newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends down on CBOT losses, exports.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends down on CBOT losses, exports.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower on Monday, in step with losses in CBOT wheat, amid poor export prospects, traders said.
"We were certainly a follower of Chicago today," one trader said.

USDA on Monday said export inspections for the week ended December 26 totalled 4.5 million bushels, well below last week's 13.5 million and the lowest weekly tally since 1982 when USDA began computerizing export records.
Volume was said to be moderate to heavy with some hedge selling noted as farmer sales picked up.
Traders said Atwood-Peavy was a seller early and Wilson Trading sold one million bushels March on the day. Benson-Quinn was said to be on both sides of the market.
White wheat futures attracted some buying interest amid ideas Pakistan would look to U.S. supplies to fill at least part of its 600,000-tonne white wheat tender.
"I think that's some of the reason white wheat firmed today," one trader said. "There was some good commercial buying interest in there."
Spring wheat ended 5-3/4 to one cent per bushel lower with March down 5-3/4 at $3.81-1/2. Barley futures did not trade.
